Dictionary

What each term and each number on the pages means, and where it comes from. The entries are in alphabetical order.

Terms

Band
The DORA level a figure falls in, from On demand to Less than once per six months, each with a score from 10 to 0.
From: Edges of the DORA Quick Check, scaled to the window.
Bot
An automated account. For commits, the author's login ends in [bot]; a login without that ending is a person's, and a commit with no login is an unknown author. For pull requests, the opener's GitHub account type is Bot, which includes every GitHub App; the type User is a person, and any other type or none is unknown, never guessed to be a person.
From: GitHub account types and logins.
Calculated at
The UTC minute the numbers were calculated at, the moment the windows were counted back from.
From: The footer of every page.
Cut
A list that GitHub gave only in part, so a figure built on it is a lower bound.
From: Page limits of the GitHub answers.
DORA
The DevOps Research and Assessment programme, whose five delivery metrics and bands forsgren follows (DORA Quick Check, dora.dev).
From: DORA Quick Check, dora.dev.
Final deployment
A deployment that ended as a success or a failure, created in the window. One still running is not stored yet, and one that ended in another way, such as a cancelled run, is not final here. It is not the last deployment: every such deployment of the window counts. Final deployments are the base of Change fail rate.
From: Deployments of data/deployments.csv.
Lead time
The time from a start to the event that finishes it. Three are told apart: deployment lead time, Lead time for changes, from a commit's author date to the successful deployment that shipped it; issue lead time, from an issue's creation to its completed close; and PR lead time, from the first commit of a pull request to its merge. Mainline Lead Time is a fourth clock, from a commit's author date to the push that brought it to main.
From: See the entries of each lead time.
Lower bound
A figure that can only be too small, never too large. Known: the commits GitHub listed for a pull request, and its merge time. Unknown: when GitHub lists only part of the commits, an earlier commit may be missing, so the first commit time may be too late. The time from it to the merge is then shorter than the true one, so the reported value is a minimum: the real value is at least this.
From: Notes below the TBD table.
Mainline
The default branch seen as a line of commits: the commits that landed on it one after another, a merge commit included, not necessarily on a branch named main. The commits of the branches merged into it are not on the line, though Mainline Lead Time counts them.
From: The default branch of each repository.
Mean
The average of the values, shown when tbd_figures is all.
From: Settings: tbd_figures.
Median
The middle value of the values; the figure the pages show by default.
From: Settings: tbd_figures.
P90
The value that nine tenths of the values are no larger than.
From: Settings: tbd_figures.
Quick Check
DORA's questionnaire (dora.dev/quickcheck, Google LLC, CC BY 4.0), in which a team picks, for each of five delivery metrics, the answer that fits best. Forsgren does not run it. It uses its answer scale: the six bands of each metric and the score of each. It checks no repository and says nothing of how a team works beyond those five metrics.
From: dora.dev.
Report Start
The first and the last minute of the window, in UTC; Report End is the Calculated at time.
From: The footer of every page.
Rework
A deployment that follows a failure: the first success after a failed deployment, or one created while a failure issue was open.
From: Deployments and failure issues.
Score
A level's number from 0 to 10 that the DORA Quick Check gives each band; the scoring view shows it.
From: DORA Quick Check, dora.dev.
Shares of commits
The TBD group of the four shares of the commits: Direct, PR, Unknown and Bots.
From: The TBD page.
Stand-in
A time used in place of an unknown one: the created time of a pull request stands in for its first commit time when no commit date can be read.
From: Pull requests of data/pulls.csv.
Stream
The deployments that follow each other in time order, grouped by repository (compared ignoring case), kind (environment, workflow or release), name (the environment or the workflow file) and task. A release has no name or task, so all releases of one repository are one stream. A failure is recovered by the next success of its own stream.
From: Deployments of data/deployments.csv.
TBD
Trunk-based development: integrating small changes into the main branch often. The TBD page shows how often, how long and how large.
From: The TBD page.
Trunk
The primary integration branch of a repository: its default branch on GitHub, whatever it is called, so not necessarily a branch named main. Trunk-based development integrates small changes into it often.
From: The default branch of each repository.
Unknown author
A commit whose author GitHub links to no account, or has the placeholder login invalid-email-address.
From: Commit authors read from GitHub.
Volume
The TBD group of the four counts Commits, Pushes, Deployments and Deployed commits.
From: The TBD page.
Window
The days the figures count back over from the time in the footer: 30, 90 or 180 days (dora_days, 30 by default).
From: dora_days in forsgren.config.yml.

Numbers

Bot PR Lead Time
The same measure as PR Lead Time, over the merged pull requests that a bot opened.
From: Merged pull requests of data/pulls.csv and data/pull_commits.csv, over the window.
Bots share
The share of the commits made by automated accounts, whose login ends in [bot]. It overlaps Direct and PR.
From: Push commits (data/push_commits.csv), over the window.
Bugs lead time
The same as the issue lead time, over the issues that carry the label bug.
From: Issue events of data/issues.csv and bug flags of data/issue_bugs.csv.
Change fail rate
The failed changes out of the final deployments, in whole percent, rounded down. A failed change is a failed deployment, or an issue labelled failure opened in the window.
From: Deployments of data/deployments.csv and issues of data/failures.csv, over the window.
Commits
On the TBD page, the commits the pushes of the window brought to the main branch, each counted once. On the Week page, shown only with week_commits: true: under Total, the row's commits of the window; under each weekday, the share of them whose author date falls on that weekday.
From: Pushes of data/pushes.csv and data/push_commits.csv, over the window.
Commits per deployment
How many commits on the main line a deployment brought; a deployment without a known main line is left out.
From: Commits of data/commits.csv and their deployments, over the window.
Commits per push
How many commits reach main in each push; a push whose commits could not be counted is left out.
From: Pushes of data/pushes.csv, over the window.
Completed
The issues closed in the period with the reason completed.
From: Issue events of data/issues.csv.
Deployed commits
The distinct commits that the deployments of the window shipped, each counted once at its first deployment.
From: Commits of data/commits.csv, over the window.
Deployment frequency
How often the project deploys successfully. The cell shows the DORA band and the number of successful deployments in the window, or in the last 180 days when the window holds none.
From: Deployments of data/deployments.csv, over the window (dora_days, 30 days by default).
Deployment rework rate
The rework deployments out of the successful ones, in whole percent, rounded down. A rework deployment is the first success after a failure, or one made while a failure issue was open.
From: Deployments of data/deployments.csv and issues of data/failures.csv, over the window.
Deployments
The successful deployments. On the Week page, Deployments under Total is the row's count of the window, and Deploys under a weekday is the share of them created on that weekday.
From: Deployments of data/deployments.csv, over the window.
Developers
The number of distinct people who authored the commits deployed in the window. A person with several email addresses counts once; bots and unknown authors are left out.
From: Commits of data/commits.csv, over the window.
Direct share
The share of the commits that did not come through a pull request, such as a commit pushed directly to main.
From: Pushes, push commits and pull requests, over the window.
Duplicate
The issues closed in the period with the reason duplicate.
From: Issue events of data/issues.csv.
Fail rate
On the Week page only, the failed deployments out of the successful plus failed ones; deployments that ended in another way are left out. Under Total, over the whole window; under each weekday, over the deployments of that weekday; a dash when there is nothing to divide. It is not the Change fail rate of the DORA table, which also counts the issues labelled failure.
From: Deployments of data/deployments.csv, over the window.
Failed deployment recovery time
The median time from the first failed deployment of a run to the next successful deployment of the same stream, with the number of recoveries in brackets.
From: Deployments of data/deployments.csv, over the window.
Failed deployments
On the Week page, the deployments with the state failure; another way of ending is not a failure. Under Total, Failed is their count in the window; under each weekday, the share of the row's failed deployments that fall on that weekday.
From: Deployments of data/deployments.csv, over the window.
Issue lead time
The median time from an issue's creation to its completed close, over the issues completed in the period.
From: Issue events of data/issues.csv.
Lead time for changes
The median time from a commit to the successful deployment that shipped it, with the number of commits deployed in the window in brackets.
From: Commits of data/commits.csv and their deployments, over the window.
Mainline Interval
The time between commits reaching the main branch, among the commits that deployments shipped. A shorter interval means changes are integrated more often.
From: Commits of data/commits.csv, over the window.
Mainline Lead Time
The time from the author date of every commit that reached main to the earliest push that brought it there, however it got there.
From: Pushes and their commits (data/pushes.csv, data/push_commits.csv) and pull requests of data/pulls.csv, over the window.
New
The issues created in the period.
From: Issue events of data/issues.csv.
Not planned
The issues closed in the period with the reason not planned.
From: Issue events of data/issues.csv.
Open
The issues open at the end of the period.
From: Issue events of data/issues.csv.
Open / Total
Open out of Total, in whole percent, rounded down; a dash when Total is 0.
From: Issue events of data/issues.csv.
Open bugs
The issues open at the end of the period that carry the GitHub label bug, as the label is at the latest collection.
From: Issue events of data/issues.csv and bug flags of data/issue_bugs.csv.
Other
The issues closed in the period with no reason, or a reason forsgren does not know.
From: Issue events of data/issues.csv.
Overall Performance
A figure from 0 to 10, to one decimal, that sums up the DORA Quick Check scores of the metrics. A metric that has data has a score: 10, 8, 6, 4, 2 or 0 for its band, or 10 minus a tenth of its whole percent for the two percent metrics. The scores of those metrics are added, each with the same weight, and divided by how many there are; an exact half rounds up. A metric with no data is left out, not scored 0, and the figure is a dash when no metric has data. It is not a DORA band: the Quick Check names none.
From: The scores of the five DORA metrics, over the window.
PR Lead Time
The time from the first commit of a pull request opened by a person to its merge.
From: Merged pull requests of data/pulls.csv and data/pull_commits.csv, over the window.
PR share
The share of the commits that came through a pull request: a merge commit of a merged pull request, or a commit that a pull request merge brought to main.
From: Pushes, push commits and pull requests, over the window.
Pushes
The pushes to the main branch.
From: Pushes of data/pushes.csv, over the window.
Time to deploy per commit
How old one change is when it is first deployed: from the author date of the commit to the first deployment that contains it.
From: Commits of data/commits.csv and their deployments, over the window.
Time to main per commit
How old one change is when it reaches the main branch: from the author date of the commit to the push that brought it to main.
From: Pushes of data/pushes.csv and data/push_commits.csv, over the window.
Total
It has three meanings. On the Issues and Daily pages, the issues created up to the end of the period, open or closed. On the Week page, the Total column group is the row's figures over the whole window. Also on the Week page, with two projects or more, the Total row is the first row and adds up the rows of every project; its shares and its Fail rate come from those sums.
From: Issue events of data/issues.csv; deployments and commits for the Week page.
Unknown share
The share of the commits whose author GitHub links to no account, or has the placeholder login invalid-email-address. It overlaps Direct and PR.
From: Push commits (data/push_commits.csv), over the window.
Weekend deployments
How many of the successful deployments that count were created on a Saturday or a Sunday (UTC). It is 0 when there are none.
From: Deployments of data/deployments.csv, over the window, or the last 180 days when the window holds no deployment.
